explanation: Players wear blackout eyeshades so everyone competes equally. The game began in 1946 to help blinded Second World War veterans, and each goal spans the court's full 9 m width.

claims.text: Goalball is a Paralympic sport in which blindfolded teams of three roll a ball containing bells towards the opposing goal.
Boccia, sitting volleyball and wheelchair rugby are not played by blindfolded teams rolling a ball with bells inside.
All goalball players wear eyeshades, so that players with different levels of sight compete equally.
Goalball was devised in 1946 as rehabilitation for visually impaired veterans of the Second World War.
A goalball court is 9 m wide, and each goal spans the full width of the court.
